_comment: ADR-037 register fragment — lti-platform-secrets-writeonly (ocon#147 phase C, openregister#380). SECURITY FIX. `signingKeys` is this instance's own rotating signing keypair(s) for the registration; each entry carries `privateKeySecret` — base64 PEM private-key material (LtiKeyService::mintKey stores it, redact() strips it before any controller return). The generic OpenRegister object API and every MCP tool over `lti_platform` read the row directly and bypass that controller redaction, so `GET /apps/openregister/api/objects/openconnector/lti_platform` returned every registration's private signing key in cleartext. Anyone holding it can mint arbitrary RFC 7523 client assertions / sign id_token launches as this instance — a key-compromise, not just a disclosure. WHY BLANKET writeOnly ON THE WHOLE `signingKeys` ARRAY rather than on `privateKeySecret` alone: `privateKeySecret` lives NESTED inside the array items, and OpenRegister resolves `writeOnly` from TOP-LEVEL schema properties only (RenderObject::getWriteOnlyProperties iterates $schema->getProperties() and matches by property name) — a marker at signingKeys[].privateKeySecret would strip nothing (silent no-op). `signingKeys` IS the top-level property, so the honest options were to promote the private key to its own top-level property (a data migration of every live registration) or this. The non-secret siblings in the array (`kid`, `algorithm`, `publicJwk`, `status`, `rotatedAt`) are not lost where they are actually used: the public JWKS is served from LtiKeyService::getPublishableJwks() which reads via _rbac: false (bypassing the writeOnly boundary), and admin key management uses dedicated #[AuthorizedAdminSetting] endpoints (LtiController::generateKey/rotateKey) that return the redacted entry. Every LtiKeyService / LtiRegistrationResolverService read already passes _rbac: false, so the launch runtime and JWKS publish keep working untouched — what the generic OR API loses is the key-lifecycle metadata, the same admin-owned-config trade the source/consumer fragments made. Paired with 99-lti-platform-lockdown.json (admin-only, since registrations are admin-owned trust anchors: issuer/clientId/jwksUri).
